nodes.label: Secondhand shopping

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_000
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: Why is there an obligation to consume second-hand clothing?
nodes.answer: PN1: Why is there an obligation to consume second-hand clothing?

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_001
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: Why do some countries still stigmatize shopping for second-hand clothes?
nodes.answer: Some countries still stigmatize shopping for second-hand clothes due to cultural norms and perceptions around used items.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_002
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: How did second-hand shopping change during the COVID-19 pandemic, according to the survey results?
nodes.answer: Second-hand shopping decreased as per the survey findings, with only 31% of respondents across seven countries reporting buying second-hand apparel pre-COVID-19.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_003
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What were some reasons for the decline in second-hand shopping during the pandemic?
nodes.answer: The decrease in second-hand shopping could be attributed to a general trend of putting all forms of consumption on hold, with some respondents mentioning they stopped buying altogether or entirely discontinued purchasing clothing.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_004
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Why did one participant in CH stop buying second-hand clothing?
nodes.answer: One participant in CH stopped buying second-hand clothing because a second-hand store near their home was closed for several months due to the pandemic.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_005
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: How did closed shops affect the practice of buying second-hand clothing?
nodes.answer: Closed physical shops meant no access to second-hand shopping altogether, leading to a decrease in engagement with this practice.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_006
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What are the potential threats that fashion rentals, vintage, and off-price items pose to traditional Canadian retailers?
nodes.answer: Fashion rentals, vintage, and off-price items could threaten traditional Canadian retailers by attracting customers who prefer the affordability and sustainability of renting or buying second-hand items. This could lead to a decrease in sales for traditional retailers who sell brand-new clothing items.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_007
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How have consumers shifted their focus from second-hand shopping to buying environmentally-friendly garments?
nodes.answer: Consumers redirected their attention due to the closure of physical second-hand stores, opting to acquire apparel sustainably by purchasing environmentally-friendly or ethically-made garments.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_008
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: How has second-hand consumption changed during the COVID-19 pandemic, according to the highlighted response from the UK?
nodes.answer: The response from the UK indicates a shift towards platforms like Depot and eBay for purchasing and selling clothes, showcasing a move away from fast fashion.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_009
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How did the pandemic impact fashion consumption practices like swapping and shopping second-hand?
nodes.answer: The pandemic led to a reduction in all forms of fashion consumption, with practices like swapping being almost completely abandoned due to physical isolation and poor online infrastructure.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_010
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: Have you ever considered using second-hand shops or online platforms for buying clothes?
nodes.answer: Yes, I frequently use second-hand shops, such as charity shops, as it allows me to find unique pieces at a lower cost.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_011
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are the barriers to second-hand consumption?
nodes.answer: Barriers to second-hand consumption include issues with returning items on time, concerns about quality, and worries about size range and accuracy of item descriptions.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_012
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How does the existence of second-hand shops in urban areas influence consumer behaviour towards fast fashion?
nodes.answer: The proximity of second-hand shops in urban areas provides consumers with alternatives to fast fashion, decreasing the need to shop at traditional retailers.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_013
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does the book "Clothing Poverty: the Hidden World of Fast Fashion and Second-hand Clothes" by Brooks, A. shed light on the fashion industry?
nodes.answer: The book sheds light on the hidden world of fast fashion and the impact of second-hand clothes on the industry.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_014
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What is the challenge in increasing consumer adoption of second-hand fashion?
nodes.answer: The challenge in increasing consumer adoption of second-hand fashion lies in the fact that while consumers are concerned about sustainable fashion, the actual number of consumers practising second-hand fashion behaviours in their purchases remains low.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_015
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How can second-hand clothing behaviours be encouraged as a sustainable alternative?
nodes.answer: Second-hand clothing behaviours can be encouraged as a sustainable alternative through examining environmental values, beliefs, and norms, which can provide insights into promoting these behaviours as a viable option to fast fashion and traditional clothing choices.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_016
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: How do concerns about environmental issues influence consumer behaviour, particularly towards second-hand fashion?
nodes.answer: Concerns about environmental issues can influence consumer behaviour towards second-hand fashion by raising awareness about sustainability and encouraging individuals to make environmentally conscious choices.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_017
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Why is the adoption of SFB limited in emerging economies?
nodes.answer: The adoption of second-hand fashion practices (SFB) is limited in emerging economies because they lack actual commercial activity promoting second-hand fashion like that seen in developed economies in Europe and the United States.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_018
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How has the second-hand market been identified as a best practice for sustainable responsibility for businesses and consumers in the fashion industry?
nodes.answer: The second-hand market has been identified as a best practice for sustainable responsibility as it promotes the circular economy by extending the lifecycle of clothing items, reducing waste, and encouraging more conscious consumption habits among consumers.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_019
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How does the bombardment of fashionable designs and attractive prices contribute to emotional obsolescence and a disposable mentality among consumers?
nodes.answer: Bombardment by successive assortment changes in fashionable designs and attractive prices, combined with dominant conventional marketing, fuels emotional obsolescence and a Ã° disposable mentality by promoting materialism and consumerism.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_020
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why were respondents willing to buy bio-based clothes but hesitant to purchase second-hand clothes?
nodes.answer: Respondents showed a positive attitude towards bio-based clothes, but they were reluctant to buy second-hand clothes due to perceiving them as poor quality, overshadowing their environmental concerns.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_021
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What percentage of Italians have purchased a fashion item from a second-hand market, according to the IPOs Report?
nodes.answer: According to the IPOs Report, only 28% of Italians have purchased a fashion item from a second-hand market.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_022
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How many traditional shops are typically devoted to the second-hand market according to the survey?
nodes.answer: The average number of traditional shops devoted to the second-hand market is 3.18.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_023
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What percentage of respondents bought second-hand clothes according to the survey findings?
nodes.answer: The survey findings show the percentage of respondents who bought second-hand clothes, as well as second-hand items, bio-based clothes, and bio-based items.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_024
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How did respondents perceive bio-based products versus second-hand clothes?
nodes.answer: Respondents viewed bio-based products as high quality and environmentally friendly, while second-hand clothes were perceived as lower quality and purchased only if assured of quality and satisfied with the price.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_025
nodes.label: Science and Tech
nodes.question: What are the coefficients for willingness to pay for bio-based and second-hand clothes in the OLS regression analysis?
nodes.answer: The coefficient for willingness to pay for bio-based clothes is 0.102 with a standard error of 0.041, while for second-hand clothes, the coefficient is 0.060 with a standard error of 0.132.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_026
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: How can second-hand clothing acquisition reflect sustainable anti-consumption mindsets?
nodes.answer: Second-hand clothing acquisition can reflect sustainable anti-consumption mindsets by increasing circulation and renewing lifespans of clothing items, thereby balancing the need for sustainable consumption practices.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Secondhand shopping_qna_027
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What is the potential downside of using second-hand clothing solely for acquiring inexpensive garments?
nodes.answer: The downside of using second-hand clothing solely for acquiring inexpensive garments is that it can lead to increased consumption and acquisition of clothes, rather than maximizing the use and lifespan of clothing items sustainably.
